title: All four ‘Lord of the Rings’ movie Hobbits explored Boston together this weekend
author: Lauren Daley
bullets: 'Lord of the Rings' actors Sean Astin, Elijah Wood, Dominic Monaghan, and Billy Boyd reunited at Fan Expo Boston.
The group dined at La Royal Cambridge and Neptune Oyster, and visited historical sites around Boston.
They also stopped at The Green Dragon pub, sharing photos and their experiences on social media.

title: Jaylen Brown to host free Boston block party at Boston Common on Aug. 30
author: Annie Jonas
bullets: Jaylen Brown to host '741 Frequency Fest' at Boston Common on August 30 for fans and residents.
The free event features music, games, and giveaways from 2 p.m. to 7 p.m. at the Charles Street entrance.
The fest celebrates Brown's 10-year tenure with the Celtics before his move to the Philadelphia 76ers.

title: Patriots reportedly releasing 2024 third-round pick Caedan Wallace
author: Hayden Bird
bullets: The Patriots are reportedly releasing offensive guard Caedan Wallace, a 2024 third-round NFL draft pick from Penn State.
Wallace played in 10 games over two seasons, with limited snaps in 2025 compared to 2024.
If released, Drake Maye and Marcellas Dial Jr. would be the only remaining 2024 Patriots draft picks on the roster.

title: Comedian Matt Rife throws down with a paranormal investigator over ‘haunted’ event in Salem
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Matt Rife faced backlash after telling a paranormal investigator to commit suicide in a comment about a Salem event.
The dispute occurred when Rife responded negatively to Chris Mac's comment about a Haunted Warren Museum event on social media.
Mac, who is autistic, and his supporters condemned Rife's remarks, calling them bullying and disgraceful.

title: Hunter Henry agrees to a two-year extension with the Patriots
author: Hayden Bird
bullets: Hunter Henry, 31, signed a two-year extension with the Patriots worth up to $20 million.
The deal includes $14.5 million in guaranteed money and a $4.2 million signing bonus.
Henry joined the Patriots in 2021 and has 259 catches and 26 touchdowns with the team.

title: 83-year-old drives Jaguar into Acton CVS, causing major damage
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: An 83-year-old woman drove a Jaguar into an Acton CVS, causing significant damage and store closure.
Neither the driver, her 88-year-old passenger, nor anyone else was injured in the Saturday afternoon crash.
Acton Police requested suspension of the driver's license, and the incident remains under investigation.

title: Logan runway closure this fall could mean more flight delays
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: Logan Airport's Runway 27 will close for 75 days starting August 31 for safety upgrades.
The project involves installing an EMAS to stop overrunning aircraft, likely causing flight delays.
Nearby communities may experience increased air traffic and construction noise during the runway closure.

title: One dead, 3 injured in head-on crash on the Cape
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: A head-on collision in Sandwich, Massachusetts, killed one person and injured three others on Sunday night.
The crash involved a westbound 2011 Toyota Prius and an eastbound 2017 Toyota RAV4 on Farmersville Road.
The Prius driver died at Cape Cod Hospital; three RAV4 occupants sustained nonlife-threatening injuries.

title: Driver on South Shore narrowly escaped before commuter train totaled his Camry
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: A 33-year-old delivery driver avoided injury after his car was hit by a MBTA Commuter Rail train in South Shore.
The driver's 2016 Toyota Camry became stuck on the tracks after a wrong turn; the train totaled the vehicle.
The crash, near Cohasset station, resulted in no injuries among the 15 passengers on board; an investigation is ongoing.

title: Livestream: Lindsay Clancy murder trial continues with psychiatrist under cross-examination
author: Abby Patkin
bullets: Lindsay Clancy's murder trial continues with psychiatrist Dr. Jennifer Tufts being cross-examined about Clancy's mental health.
Tufts testified Clancy denied having suicidal or homicidal thoughts before killing her three children in January 2023.
Clancy claims postpartum mental illness, using an insanity defense, and cites voice commands to explain her actions.
